### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s).

**22** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a2f523aa36155385da59b2ef3cbdf8ee336747d5`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **222** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **159** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **159**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **36** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a2f523aa36155385da59b2ef3cbdf8ee336747d5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3359f5074dadad68ae98d0f01856dc2e7bde78e4` — the merge of head `1764b50e8474d94eaa7a521dd97ce3e33bb52018` into base `a2f523aa36155385da59b2ef3cbdf8ee336747d5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3359f5074dadad68ae98d0f01856dc2e7bde78e4 && git checkout 3359f5074dadad68ae98d0f01856dc2e7bde78e4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a2f523aa36155385da59b2ef3cbdf8ee336747d5 1764b50e8474d94eaa7a521dd97ce3e33bb52018 && git checkout -B drift-repro a2f523aa36155385da59b2ef3cbdf8ee336747d5 && git merge --no-ff 1764b50e8474d94eaa7a521dd97ce3e33bb52018

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a2f523aa36155385da59b2ef3cbdf8ee336747d5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a2f523aa36155385da59b2ef3cbdf8ee336747d5` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Contract review for card #30771 · narrowing face (`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`) · read-only reviewer at the contract-review tier, brief per `record-recognisers --brief-template --face narrowing` · 2026-11-06T06:52Z

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8b3369861b34ea14e11486c75beef344c84a648c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/platform-objects/src/identity/platform-admin-action-gate.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-member.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-oauth-application.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-sso-provider.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/platform-admin-affordance-standing.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/api-action-door-forward.dogfood.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/mcp-system-object-action-exposure.dogfood.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/api-action-create-user-email-param.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/platform-admin-action-gate.test.ts + packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts (`actionPermissionError`, `invokeBusinessAction`), packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts (REST door), packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts (`listActions`, `runAction`, `resumeAdmissionRefusal`), packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts (`isListableAction`, `run_action`), packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts (§6b, §6b-config, §6d), packages/core/src/security/assemble-execution-context.ts (agent `systemPermissions`), packages/spec/src/identity/eval-user.zod.ts (`ADMIN_FULL_ACCESS_CAPABILITIES`), packages/spec/src/security/capabilities.ts (`PLATFORM_CAPABILITIES`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/platform-admin-gate.ts and auth-manager-before-hook.ts and auth-route-ledger.ts (the target doors), docs/adr/0066 D4, content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx. Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on body and changeset; no governed path, no published schema in the diff).

Inputs read: card #30771 body and all six comments (triage 6675600532, claims 6677617495 and 6677709499, priority 6678665567, os-dev-report 6678862496), the ruling it cites (6674432613, row 16 letter A, with the seat analysis 6671252245), PR #30849 body, its 11-file list, the net diff against `main`, and the 47 check-runs on the head. Check-runs as read: 23 success, 13 skipped, 11 in progress (Build Core, Test Core 1-4 and 6-8, Type Check consumer gates and workspace, Live E2E UI); no failure. Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates and Lint · PM dispatch-gates are green.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The population is the family, no door missed — right.** `platform-admin-affordance-standing.test.ts` on `main` derives the family as every first-party action whose `target` is in `/api/v1/auth/admin/` minus `has-permission` and `stop-impersonating`, plus `/api/v1/auth/organization/add-member`. A grep of every `target:` under `packages/**/*.object.ts` on `main` finds exactly 15 such targets: `sys_user` 8 (ban, unban, unlock, create-user, set-user-password, impersonate, set-user-manager, list-platform-admins), `sys_member.add_member`, `sys_oauth_application` 2 (`toggle-disabled` twice), `sys_sso_provider` 4. The test's floor list names 14; the 15th (`list_platform_admins`) joins by its target. Every other `/organization/*` target (invite, remove-member, update-member-role, create, delete, teams) is judged by the vendor's org-role or a before-hook guard, not by the platform-admin judge, so none belongs here. Nothing outside the diff declares one of these targets.
2. **Each of the 15 is really a platform-admin door — right.** The raw `/admin/*` mounts, `set-user-manager`, `list-platform-admins`, `impersonate` and the `oauth2/toggle-disabled` mount call `judgePlatformAdmin` (plugin-auth `platform-admin-gate.ts`); `/sso/register` and `register-saml` are judged by the before-hook's `isPlatformAdminUserId`; `organization/add-member` is recorded in `auth-route-ledger.ts` as "platform-admin gated (ADR-0068)". The `visible` predicate on all 15 already reads the rung.
3. **The two gate names are right, and a rung holder keeps every one of the 15.** `manage_users` and `manage_platform_settings` are both in `ADMIN_FULL_ACCESS_CAPABILITIES.systemPermissions` and both `scope: 'platform'` in `PLATFORM_CAPABILITIES`. Both anchors of the rung put that list on the holder: the grant anchor via the catalog body of `admin_full_access` folded at §6b (a code-package set, `not_overridable`), the config anchor via the explicit push at §6b-config. A deactivated `admin_full_access` confers neither the rung nor the caps, so hidden-and-refused stays consistent. The new standing-test case pins every declared name against both lists, with a positive control on the two names. The users/settings split is cosmetic to the gate (every rung holder holds both) and reads well as documentation.
4. **Accept-set changes, each named.** MCP `list_actions`: from every authenticated caller to holders of the capability (the `actionPermissionError` filter at mcp.ts line 878 already exists on `main`; the diff adds no runtime code). `POST /actions/:object/:action`, MCP `run_action` by name, `resume_run`: from forwarded-then-target-403 to door-403 with the capability sentence, nothing forwarded. MCP `run_action` with `objectName`: tool-layer system-object refusal (see ④ S1). A caller whose only standing is the legacy `role === 'admin'` scalar: from admitted at the target to refused at the doors (judged in ④). Console: unchanged, because `visible` already reads the rung and the D4 UI half (`useConsoleActionRuntime`) reads `requiredPermissions` fail-open; the changeset's "as before" claim holds.
5. **Agent principals — no new class refused.** `assemble-execution-context.ts` gives an agent the delegating user's whole `systemPermissions` under `actions:execute` and `[]` without it; without it the forward was already refused by `apiForwardCredentialRefusal` rule 1. The dogfood pins for the admin's agent (E and confirmed C) are unchanged and reported green.
6. **Public surface — none moves.** `identity/index.ts` is untouched, so the two constants are package-internal; the only published package the diff moves is `@objectstack/platform-objects`. `api-action-create-user-email-param.test.ts`'s fixture now holds the rung's capabilities, which is what its docblock already claimed the caller was.
7. **Residual named, not a narrowing.** A holder of `manage_users` without the rung (a custom set, or `admin_full_access` under a walled posture where §6b confers the set's caps but not standing) is listed and then refused by the target, exactly as before this PR. The acceptance notes say so; it is the inherent limit of a capability standing in for a rung no key can name, and the ruling's "list only what the caller can run" is met for every first-party standing.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/platform-objects': patch` is right: `Metadata-protocol: none` (an existing ADR-0066 D4 key, no spec change, no authorable surface added or removed), and a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its BREAKING banner. The PR body and the changeset both carry `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial; the banner `**BREAKING.**` is present; the title carries `!`; exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), which is right because nothing an author wrote is retired or renamed; the one upgrader action (a grant or `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL`) is stated in the changeset's third bullet, which ships in `CHANGELOG.md`. No `skip-changeset`. Check Changeset is green. The expected shape (`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, BREAKING banner, `!` title) is met.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Two dogfood files outside the claim surface — accepted.** They are the standing pins of exactly the two doors this narrowing changes, and their old assertions ("passes the door and is refused by the identity route") became false by the ruling's own intent. Editing the pin of the behaviour one changes is the Post-Task rule, not scope creep. Both rewrites keep the safety half (nobody banned, status 403 on REST, anonymous 401).
2. **MCP `run_action` with `objectName` answers the system-object sentence, not the capability sentence — escalated as should-fix S1 in ④.** The dev's "accurate but less precise" is not accurate: the sentence says the action "is not exposed via MCP" and names `ai.exposed`, which is false for `ban_user` (`ai.exposed: true`); the real cause is the caller's grant.
3. **Before/now prose instead of a literal FROM → TO — accepted.** `check-adr-0087-registration` reads that label as a migration prescription and would refuse the `not-required` disposition; the migration content (grant or env var) is in the changeset in plain words, and the FROM → TO form is in the PR body. The marker's reasoning is right.
4. **`invite_user` declared four times — accepted.** Four distinct `(objectName, name)` addresses on one target, `/organization/invite-member`, which is not a platform-admin door and so is outside this narrowing; `run_action` refuses an ambiguous bare name. Correctly measured and left alone.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing against the published spec on `main`.** The spec's platform-admin standing is the rung: ADR-0095 D3 and `resolve-authz-context.ts` §6d resolve the posture "from held CAPABILITY grants — never from a better-auth role"; ADR-0068 D2 derives `platform_admin` from the anchoring `admin_full_access` grant; plugin-auth `platform-admin-gate.ts` keeps `user.role === 'admin'` "ONLY as the legacy fallback it has always been here", re-synthesis vetoed by the maintainer on 2026-08-18. ADR-0066 D4 (amended 2026-10-29) says the platform action door runs the declared-capability gate before forwarding and the target must still enforce itself, "the door's gate being the added check: defence in depth, not a replacement". So:

- **The legacy `role === 'admin'` caller without the rung: the spec's own refusal made real, not a taken-away capability.** That caller holds no declared capability anywhere in the spec; it is admitted at the vendor-adjacent targets by a back-compat fallback the gate's own header calls legacy. The console already denies it these buttons (`visible` reads the rung, which the session emits from grants). What this PR closes is the one path where a declared gate was absent and the fallback leaked through: REST `/actions` and MCP. The target endpoints keep the fallback, so the deployment is not locked out, and the changeset names the one-line fix. This is the ruling's intent as the seat's claim amendment (6677709499) stated it before the dev built: "A legacy `role==='admin'` caller without the platform-admin rung is now refused at the door. BREAKING banner; the maintainer's per-PR word is owed before landing." Judged right. The maintainer's word on the BREAKING is still owed and is not this record's to give.
- **One reader, one `ec`, listed if and only if runnable at the gate — holds.** `listActions` (mcp.ts line 878), `runAction` → `invokeBusinessAction` (action-execution.ts line 4323), `resumeAdmissionRefusal` (mcp.ts line 1324) and the REST door (actions.ts line 652) all call `actionPermissionError` on the same declaration with the same assembled context; the listing omits `objectName` from the call, which changes only the sentence, never the verdict. The gate runs before the type branch, the param contract and the record load on every door. The new runtime test pins the agreement per action for two callers against the real `sys_user` declaration through the production bridge and `handleActions`, with the forward target faked so "never forwarded" is observed, not inferred. Pre-existing non-agreements (a disabled action is listed and refused 409; a credential-refused forward is listed with `unavailable`) are unchanged by this diff.
- **Tried and not broken.** `isSystem` bypass: a system caller passes the door and the target judges, as before. Deactivated anchor set: no caps and no rung, consistent. Walled posture: caps without rung is the residual in ①.7, as before. Handler-owner gate (action-execution.ts line 5172): irrelevant for `type: 'api'`. The standing test derives from source files, so the "every member declares" pin cannot be satisfied vacuously; its positive control fails if either name leaves `ADMIN_FULL_ACCESS_CAPABILITIES`.

**S1 — should-fix: the scoped MCP refusal names a false cause.** `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts` `run_action` (lines 1695–1703) admits a `sys_*` action with `objectName` only where the bridge's listing lists it; since the listing is now permission-filtered, a plain member calling `run_action` with `objectName: 'sys_user'` is answered `systemObjectActionRefusal`: "is not exposed via MCP: a system object's action is reachable only when its author exposed it to AI (ai.exposed) and list_actions lists it for you". For the 15 actions this is untrue (all are `ai.exposed: true`) and it points the agent at the author instead of at the caller's grant; a refusal that misnames its cause is the wrong-prescription class the refusal-prose rule and Route & surface ownership rule 4 exist for. The shape predates this PR, but this PR is the first to route a whole family through it and pins the sentence in `mcp-system-object-action-exposure.dogfood.test.ts`. The dev reported it "noted, not filed"; a reproducible wrong-cause refusal is Prime Directive 10's file-an-issue class, and `packages/mcp/src/**` is inside the claim's file surface, so either an in-PR fix (ask the bridge whether the action is unlisted for exposure or for permission, and answer the capability sentence with 403 in the second case) or a filed card is owed before landing. Not a FAIL: the call is refused with nothing forwarded, the by-name path answers the capability sentence with its status, and the ruling's substance (one declaration, read by the listing and both doors) is delivered.

No must-fix found.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1764b50e8474d94eaa7a521dd97ce3e33bb52018`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-action-system-object-exposure.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/runtime/src/platform-admin-action-gate.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/mcp-system-object-action-exposure.dogfood.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/api-action-door-forward.dogfood.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/platform-admin-action-gate.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-member.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-oauth-application.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-sso-provider.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/platform-admin-affordance-standing.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/api-action-create-user-email-param.test.ts + packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts (REST door, line 652), packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts (`error`), packages/runtime/src/error-envelope.ts (`buildApiError`), packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts (`StandardErrorCode`, `HttpStatusErrorCodeMap`, `standardErrorCodeForHttpStatus`), packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts (owner keys `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/mcp`, the provenance rule), packages/spec/scripts/check-error-code-provenance.ts, scripts/check-error-status-conformance.mjs, scripts/check-dispatcher-error-vocabulary.mjs, content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx (the 403 row), .github/workflows/ci.yml (`dogfood`, `dogfood-gate`), packages/qa/dogfood/test/parent-read-gate-silent-skip.dogfood.test.ts and packaged-action-disabled-dispatch-live.dogfood.test.ts and mcp-oauth-api-action-forward.dogfood.test.ts (reach of the delta). Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on body and changeset; no governed path, no published schema in the diff).

Delta record over 6679092098 (PASS on `8b3369861b34ea14e11486c75beef344c84a648c`, one should-fix S1). Inputs read: the compare `8b336986...1764b50e` (one commit, dated 2026-11-06, seven files: the changeset, mcp-http-tools.ts and its exposure test, action-execution.ts, domains/mcp.ts, the runtime gate test, the MCP dogfood file), the net diff against `main` (15 files), card #30771 with all six comments (no comment after the claim 6678953801; ruling A 6674432613 and the seat analysis 6671252245 re-read), the rewritten PR body, the docs-drift comment 6678866422, and the check-runs on the new head. Check-runs as read, second read: 51 total, 26 success, 15 skipped, 10 in progress (Test Core 1-4 and 6-8, Build Core, Type Check workspace and consumer gates); no failure. Green: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, every Lint lane (ESLint, docs & code guards, repo & tooling gates, CI/release/engine gates, PM dispatch-gates, the three scoped lanes), Type Check debt ledger and source gates, Spec property liveness, Test Core 5/8, Test UI, Live E2E UI, the PR-body guards, and the aggregate Dogfood Regression Gate (see ④ S2 for what that one attests). The unchanged findings of the prior record (①.1 to ①.7, ③.1, ③.3, ③.4, and ④'s judgment of the narrowing against the published spec) are carried forward as they stand; the delta touches none of the declarations, the REST door, the listing filter or the standing test they were made on.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **S1 is closed: scoped and by-name answer one refusal, nothing runs.** `run_action` (mcp-http-tools.ts lines 1712-1725) enters the pre-screen only for `objectName` on a `sys_*` object and only when the listing does not admit the pair; there it asks `bridge.capabilityRefusal?.(actionName, objectName)` and renders a non-undefined answer through `errorResultWithCode`, else the system-object sentence; both returns precede `bridge.runAction`. The runtime bridge (domains/mcp.ts lines 912-923) answers from `collectActionDeclarations` over the same `getMeta`, `readServedObjects`, `readServedActions` the listing reads, finds the one `(objectName, name)` declaration, returns undefined for not-declared, for `systemObjectActionExposureError` and for `actionAiExposureError`, and otherwise `actionPermissionRefusal(deps, found.action, ec, objectName)`. The sentence is `actionPermissionError` with `objectName`, which is exactly what `invokeBusinessAction` passes by name (line 4346, the resolved `objectName`), so the two strings are one function's output on one declaration and one `ec`. Pinned three ways: the runtime test holds `refusal.message === thrown.message` per pinned action with the forward never called; the MCP unit test renders the bridge's answer as `{ code: 'PERMISSION_DENIED', status: 403, message }` with `bridge.runs` empty; the dogfood holds `messageOf(scoped) === messageOf(byName)`, both `PERMISSION_DENIED` 403, neither matching "is not exposed via MCP", and `isBanned === false`. The CONTROL unexposed action keeps the sentence: `impersonate_user` declares `requiredPermissions: [...PLATFORM_ADMIN_USERS_GATE]` (sys-user.object.ts line 487) and no `ai` block, so the bridge returns undefined at the system-object check and the tool answers the system-object sentence; pinned in the runtime test (undefined) and the dogfood (the sentence). The prior record's prescription ("ask the bridge whether the action is unlisted for exposure or for permission, and answer the capability sentence with 403 in the second case") is implemented as written.
2. **The new wire shape is not a vocabulary widening; it is the surface's existing coded-refusal carrier applied to one more refusal.** Before: `invokeBusinessAction` threw `new Error(gateError)`; `errorResultFromThrown` found no code and answered the bare sentence. Now the throw carries `code: standardErrorCodeForHttpStatus(403)` and `status: 403`, and `errorResultFromThrown` (line 469) routes `PERMISSION_DENIED` through `errorResultWithCode` to `codedErrorResult`, the `{ error: { code, message, status } }` text the tool already answers for `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` 428, `ACTION_DISABLED` 409 and the record-level security gate's own `PERMISSION_DENIED` (that arm exists on `main`). `PERMISSION_DENIED` is a `StandardErrorCode` member and `HttpStatusErrorCodeMap[403]` (errors.zod.ts lines 79 and 186); it has no row under any ledger owner key (the only mentions in error-code-ledger.zod.ts are a comment at line 1491 and the `FORBIDDEN` waiver's `shadows`), and `check:error-code-provenance` sweeps "every stamp site of a REGISTERED code" (ledger header, the #13353 paragraph), so it demands no row for `@objectstack/runtime` or `@objectstack/mcp`. The spelling `code: standardErrorCodeForHttpStatus(403)` already stands twice in action-execution.ts on `main` (lines 1832 and 1847) and domains/mcp.ts line 1010 stamps the literal, under a green `Lint · repo & tooling gates` on this head, which carries the dispatcher-vocabulary gate. `check:error-status-conformance` direction A asks that every emitted status for a code be documented: error-catalog.mdx publishes 403 for `PERMISSION_DENIED` (the quick-reference row at line 999), and the deriver reads the rest and types error classes, the `sendError` doors and the map, not a runtime object literal; the gate is green on this head. The changeset declares the shape in its own paragraph and bumps `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/mcp` `patch`, with `Metadata-protocol: none` and the single `Clause-②` arm kept (AGENTS.md Post-Task 3: at most one arm; the narrowing is the breaking half and dominates, the additive half is named in prose). The reach is every action with `requiredPermissions`, not only the 15, which the changeset and the PR body both say.
3. **Within ruling A and the claim surface.** Ruling A: "REST `/actions` and MCP read it from one place"; the delta adds no second reading, it makes the MCP tool layer's scoped refusal read the same `actionPermissionError` the other three doors read.
